# NOTES ON "THOMAS WINGFOLD, CURATE" (George MacDonald, 2 volumes in the source; text includes Vol II then Vol I)

Note on framing: the source file's system/user scaffolding (CLAUDE.md, env, etc.) is not part of the novel and is ignored here.

## BOOK 1 of 2: Vol. II (Gutenberg 5974)

**Ch I, Rachel and her Uncle.** Dusk, Rachel opens gate for Miss Lingard and rider (no thanks). Rachel envies Miss Lingard's strength/height. Uncle Polwarth: content vs satisfied, "grumble vs prayer"; hope of redemption of body. Rachel jokes about "little crooked shadow" in churchyard. Dives/Lazarus reference. Polwarth on self-consciousness "like the onliness of God." Rachel: "I should like to be made over again." Polwarth offers to read verses; Rachel wants Wingfold to hear; she is temperamental and repents by kissing his hand. Polwarth kisses her forehead; she won't go up stairs before him. Wingfold arrives; Rachel goes down to receive him.

**Ch II, A Dream.** Polwarth reads his poem (Lord, hear my discontent; "I am the door..."; "Thou only thinkest--I am thought"). Wingfold asks to take verses; Polwarth will copy them. Wingfold asks about Bible inspiration; Polwarth: "highest means of spiritual education... the man Christ Jesus." Polwarth's dream: Tauchnitz edition of English NT with Sinaitic manuscript (found by Tischendorf, Mount Sinai); asthma; desert journey to Armenian convent to find St John's original gospel; monastery door, cell, curtain torn; an old beloved disciple burns the book, saying "the Word of God liveth... in the heart of the man that in love obeyeth him." Wingfold: "I trust I have the lesson too."

**Ch III, Another Sermon.** Wingfold's first thoughts now his own; crowds come. Second sermon: Christianity = what is of Christ in you; "I dare not call myself a Christian"; subscribed Articles unthinkingly. Texts: love enemies, be perfect, lay not up treasure, take no thought, judge not, golden rule, "Not everyone that saith Lord, Lord."

**Ch IV, Nursing.** Mrs Ramshorn (dean's widow) calls sermon pagan; Bascombe: "I like the fellow... great rubbish." Helen, who nurses Leopold (drug habit; dejection; Mr Faber the doctor; Leopold's nightmares; "Give me my knife. Why will you not let me die?"). Grimm tale rejected; Thousand and One Nights read.

**Ch V, Glaston and the Curate.** Town gossip about Wingfold's oddity (sunstroke, vanity, fanatic, Romanizer). Poem "O Lord, if on the wind..." Bascombe calls him hypochondriac.

**Ch VI, The Linen-Draper.** Mr Drew, chief linen-draper, middle-aged, plump, pug-nosed, black eyes; wife left him with a travelling man (~20 years ago; daughter of a doctor). Drew confesses unjust dealings; sermon "How would Jesus have done as a draper?" Wingfold: "Jesus buying and selling". Wingfold urges prayer.

**Ch VII, Rachel.** Wingfold asks Polwarth to bring Drew to tea. Rachel's room: all white; she talks of being "a little sheep" on the altar; dreams of freedom; dreams of flowers ("haemony" in Comus); "I NEVER dream of being crooked." Polwarth's brother (Rachel's father) wrote a manuscript.

**Ch VIII, The Butterfly.** Wingfold's thoughts on nature, God; sonnet "Methought I floated sightless..."

**Ch IX, The Common-place.** Drew's shop at evening: sells soldiers' wives cloth at cost; his reflections (wife, self-preservation, hymn "Let me stand ever at the door"); "shop as temple"; Drew will give up deaconship, keep pew and subscription.

**Ch X, Home Again.** Meets Bascombe; Wingfold says he'll keep appointment; "But if what I find should be true." Sonnet "Methought that in a solemn church I stood." Churchyard "curate's chair."

**Ch XI, The Sheath.** Polwarth tells of night in park, cry from old house of Glaston (uninhabited 20 years); woman and youth in closet; Polwarth found no one but a bed; gives Wingfold a small leather knife sheath. Helen's face comes to Wingfold's mind.

**Ch XII, Invitation.** Wingfold reflects on human suffering; "COME UNTO ME ALL YE THAT LABOUR..."

**Ch XIII, A Sermon to Helen.** Wingfold preaches on Matthew 11:28 ("Come unto me..."), Helen weeps. Bascombe irritated.

**Ch XIV, A Sermon to Himself.** Sonnet-poem "Yes, Master, when thou comest..." Helen sobs.

**Ch XV, Criticism.** Mrs Ramshorn, Bascombe, Helen argue after church; Bascombe's anti-religious speech (Lord Jesus "old Jew fable"); "vivisection." Helen's anger.

**Ch XVI, A Vanishing Glimmer.** Helen tells Leopold about the sermon; Leopold: "She is DEAD--I killed her." Leopold reveals "The jury!"; wants death; Helen's bitterness.

**Ch XVII, Let Us Pray!** Helen plans to consult Wingfold; Leopold: "Helen, what HAVE I done..."; Helen's "Sandwich Islands" fantasy; sings "Come unto me" defiantly.

**Ch XVIII, Two Letters.** Helen's letter to Wingfold asking meeting; he proposes cottage meeting at Polwarths'. Helen meets him at honeysuckle seat in Polwarth garden.

**Ch XIX, Advice in the Dark.** Helen asks about "a great wrong"; Wingfold advises confession; Helen faints-near; "At least confession--" Wingfold rises.

**Ch XX, Intercession.** Helen faints; Polwarth prays; Helen flees home.

**Ch XXI, Helen Alone.** Helen in summer-house; despises Wingfold; prays.

**Ch XXII, A Haunted Soul.** Leopold sees Emmeline's ghost in mirror, worm on shoulder; "if you don't let me see Mr. Wingfold, I shall go mad."

**Ch XXIII, Compelled Confidence.** Helen fetches Wingfold; in park she demands he not counsel surrender; Wingfold shows knife sheath; Helen: "Give it me... It is mine."

**Ch XXIV, Willing Confidence.** Leopold confesses to Wingfold; embraces him. "Emmeline" dream; Leopold wants to die/be hanged.

**Ch XXV, The Curate's Counsel.** Wingfold: "Jesus... COME UNTO ME"; "Shame is not defilement."

**Ch XXVI, Sleep.** Leopold sleeps; "Did God make me sleep?" Helen jealous; Leopold: met Helen when he came to England.

**Ch XXVII, Divine Service.** Polwarth and Drew talk; "shop is the temple"; Polwarth on divine service as communion.

**Ch XXVIII, A Shop in Heaven.** Rachel reads Polwarth's vision: ideal city of trade where no money passes; the man who prayed on kneeling.

**Ch XXIX, Polwarth and Lingard.** Leopold wants to confess; "I wish to give myself up"; Helen begs; Wingfold and Polwarth stay; Leopold faints. Men leave.

**Ch XXX, The Strong Man.** Bascombe visits Leopold; plans to take him to Mr Hooker (magistrate) on Monday; Bascombe suspects Wingfold.

**Ch XXXI, George and Leopold.** Bascombe's advice on hanging; Wingfold visits, turned away. Bascombe thinks about Helen.

**Ch XXXII, Wingfold and Helen.** Helen comes to library; Wingfold: "Love your brother aright"; "let your pride die for him." Helen angry.

**Ch XXXIII, A Review.** Wingfold's churchyard reflections; poem "Father, I cry to thee for bread."

**Ch XXXIV, A Sermon to Leopold.** Sermon: "I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance." Ends Vol II.

## BOOK 2 of 2: Vol. I (Gutenberg 5973)

**Ch I, Helen Lingard.** November wind; Helen 23, tall, blue-eyed, dark-haired; bored; reads novel; sleeps till tea. Brother Leopold at Cambridge. Father an officer in India with Hindoo wife; Leopold a half-Indian boy; Helen's mother died at her birth; aunt (Mrs Ramshorn) raised her.

**Ch II, Thomas Wingfold.** Wingfold walks in Osterfield park; river; ferns; Horace "quam memento" ode; 26 years old; ordained; uncle D.D. (Jonah Driftwood).

**Ch III, The Diners.** Mrs Ramshorn (widow of Dean of Halystone); cousin George Bascombe (son of her sister, barrister, Havannah cigars); Wingfold (about 30, grey eyes, black hair). Dinner talk: poetry, Horace, Bascombe's song "Each man has his lampful..."

**Ch IV, Their Talk.** Bascombe's views; Helen plays piano woodenly.

**Ch V, A Staggering Question.** Church tower in moonlight; Bascombe: "Do you believe one word of all that?" Wingfold can't answer.

**Ch VI, The Curate in the Churchyard.** Wingfold sits on gravestone ("curate's chair") doubting.

**Ch VII, The Cousins.** Bascombe's character (prophet of destroying beliefs); Helen's character.

**Ch VIII, The Garden.** Bascombe and Helen talk in Mrs Ramshorn's garden; Bascombe's philosophy of death.

**Ch IX, The Park.** Walk in park; the old house of Glaston (lake, garden, closet, trap-well); legend of lady drowned in sack.

**Ch X, The Dwarfs.** Bascombe sneers at Rachel and Polwarth (deformed); eugenic views; Sunday sermon on forgiveness. Helen loves Leopold.

**Ch XI, The Curate at Home.** Wingfold's spiritual crisis; prays and doubts; sermons from his uncle's collection.

**Ch XII, An Incident.** Wingfold finds Rachel's manuscript on stile; "Do not be alarmed: I have not read one word of it."

**Ch XIII, A Report of Progress.** Bascombe courts Helen; she is mildly amused.

**Ch XIV, Jeremy Taylor.** Letter from Joseph Polwarth: Wingfold's sermon was Jeremy Taylor's.

**Ch XV, The Park Gate.** Wingfold visits Polwarths at Park Gate lodge; Rachel answers door.

**Ch XVI, The Attic.** Polwarth's room under eaves; books; advice on sermons.

**Ch XVII, Polwarth's Plan.** Polwarth: preach honest; asks "Was there such a man as Jesus?" Rachel present.

**Ch XVIII, Joseph Polwarth.** Polwarth's life: Cornish ancestors, gambling; school bullying; boy in pond; New Testament Matthew 1:21 converted him ("he shall save his people from their sins").

**Ch XIX, The Conclusion of the Whole Matter.** Polwarth: "Take your New Testament... and read--to find out." Wingfold will try.

**Ch XX, A Strange Sermon.** Wingfold's confessional sermon: "Confessing your faults one to another"; reads quotations from old divines.

**Ch XXI, A Thunderbolt.** Helen at window at midnight; Leopold appears with blood on wristband; "I am a murderer, and they are after me." Helen hides him.

**Ch XXII, Leopold.** Helen swears to protect him ("So help me God"). Leopold's knife with name engraved. Leopold hides under bed. Helen takes him to old house.

**Ch XXIII, The Refuge.** Old house; Leopold in hidden room, horror at closet; "Can you whistle, Helen?" Leopold has a knife, drug in silver box.

**Ch XXIV, Helen with a Secret.** Helen's guilty dread; dissimulation; daylight.

**Ch XXV, A Daylight Visit.** Helen prays "I am his sister, thou knowest!"; visits Leopold; passes Rachel singing.

**Ch XXVI, Leopold's Story.** Emmeline (manufacturer's eldest daughter, flaxen-haired); Captain Hodges; Leopold's drug use; Emmeline's manipulation.

**Ch XXVII, Leopold's Story Concluded.** Masked ball; Leopold passes note "Meet me for one long minute at the circle"; Emmeline: "I am going to be married to Captain Hodges"; Leopold stabs her with a skean-dhu; flees to coal-pit shaft; comes to Helen's window.

**Ch XXVIII, Sisterhood.** Helen: "I would rather be you than she"; Helen takes knife; sisterly devotion.

**Ch XXIX, The Sick-Chamber.** Helen brings Leopold to her room; aunt helps; Mr Faber (new doctor) diagnoses brain-fever; Helen nurses. Helen's new sense of life.

**Ch XXX, The Curate's Progress.** Wingfold studies NT with Polwarth; Polwarth prays for him. Parish complaints about Wingfold's gleaned sermons.

**Ch XXXI, The Curate Makes a Discovery.** "Why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?" Wingfold confesses in pulpit: "I dare not call myself a Christian." Helen in congregation.

**Ch XXXII, Hopes.** Leopold asks for Bascombe; Helen doubts Leopold's guilt; Helen agrees to ride with George.

**Ch XXXIII, The Ride.** Helen and Bascombe ride in park toward the old house; Bascombe on immortality and murder case (girl in ball-dress, stabbed to heart; coastguard saw boat; Holland). Helen gasps; "We must get him out of the country." Bascombe: "Every murderer hanged... is a gain to the community." Ends Vol I.
